model_name: Repressilator: symmetric six-variable transcriptional oscillator (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1)
description: Deterministic continuous 'repressilator' model of a synthetic cyclic negative-feedback loop in E. coli. Six coupled ODEs describe the 3 repressor mRNAs (m_lacI, m_tetR, m_cI) and their 3 proteins (p_lacI, p_tetR, p_cI). Transcription of each mRNA is repressed by the protein of the previous gene in the cycle (LacI represses tetR; TetR represses cI; CI represses lacI) through a Hill function 1/(1+p_j^n) plus a leak term a0; translation is represented by the linear coupling b*(m_i) and both species decay linearly. Time is rescaled to the mRNA lifetime, protein concentrations in units of K_M (repressors needed for half-maximal repression) and mRNA in units of translation efficiency.

variables.name: m_lacI
variables.description: lacI mRNA concentration (rescaled by translation efficiency)

variables.name: m_tetR
variables.description: tetR mRNA concentration (rescaled by translation efficiency)

variables.name: m_cI
variables.description: cI mRNA concentration (rescaled by translation efficiency)

variables.name: p_lacI
variables.description: LacI repressor protein concentration (units of K_M)

variables.name: p_tetR
variables.description: TetR repressor protein concentration (units of K_M)

variables.name: p_cI
variables.description: CI repressor protein concentration (units of K_M)

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Effective maximal transcription rate (promoter strength x translation efficiency / (mRNA decay rate^2 x K_M)). Derived from the paper's values: induced promoter strength 0.5 transcripts/s, translation 20 proteins/transcript (=0.1667 s^-1), mRNA half-life 2 min, K_M=40. Equals 'alpha', the maximum proteins per cell (x K_M).

parameters.name: a0
parameters.description: Leakiness: residual transcription with saturating repressor. Derived from the paper's repressed promoter strength 5e-4 transcripts/s; note a0/a = 1e-3, exactly the ratio used for curve C in Fig. 1b.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Ratio of protein decay rate to mRNA decay rate, from protein half-life 10 min and mRNA half-life 2 min (120/600 = 0.2). In the paper's stability diagram this is the parameter beta.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Hill coefficient of cooperativity of repression (paper: n = 2)

origin.source_text: Elowitz, M. B. & Leibler, S. 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403, 335-338 (2000). Box 1 'Network design', deterministic continuous approximation.
assumptions: Symmetric case: all three repressors are treated as identical except for their DNA-binding specificity (same a, a0, b, n).
Well-mixed, continuous, deterministic approximation; molecular discreteness and stochasticity (treated separately by the paper's stochastic simulation) are neglected.
Transcription depends on the repressor through a Hill function 1/(1+p^n); promoter leakiness a0 adds a constant basal transcription.
Translation and protein decay are lumped into the linear term -b(p_i - m_i).
Time rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime; protein concentrations in units of K_M; mRNA rescaled by translation efficiency. 1 time unit = 2 min.

missing_information: The paper does not state the explicit initial conditions used for the numerical integration in Fig. 1c; the non-symmetric values used here are an arbitrary (but documented) choice needed to start the simulation off the symmetric manifold. Because the solution converges to a limit cycle, the long-time behaviour is independent of these values.
The exact numeric solution values (period/amplitude) behind Fig. 1c are not tabulated in the text; only the qualitative result 'sustained limit-cycle oscillations' is reported.

The axis label of Fig. 1b reads 'Protein lifetime/mRNA lifetime, beta', which is ambiguous; the equation dpi/dt = -b(pi - mi) implies b is the ratio of DECAY RATES (0.2 from the stated half-lives). This ambiguity is flagged here.
